answer: A practical defense is a stake-and-history bond: before an agent may wander into shared marketplaces, it must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable record of honest work. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, and misbehavior forfeits the bond, like a lotus that only blooms after long, costly cultivation, not overnight. A sybil farmer faces a mesa of rising marginal cost: each extra identity needs another deposit, another history, and another risk of slashing, so mass forgery stops paying while honest agents keep operating cheaply.
